observation.visible_scene: An outdoor basketball court with a single hoop, backboard and support pole standing on a reddish court surface, grass and trees behind. A person in a pale t‑shirt and black shorts is positioned right at the pole, holding a basketball near the rim at the start and, over the excerpt, guiding that ball upward so it climbs in front of the backboard while the person's body lowers toward the ground.
visible_changes: At t=0 the person is airborne with one knee raised and both hands on the ball at rim height; the ball sits just left of the hoop.
The person's raised knee lowers and both feet drop toward the court surface, so the body transitions from a suspended/jumping pose to a more upright, grounded stance by the middle of the clip.
The grip on the ball changes from two hands to one extended arm; the torso rotates from a near back‑on view to a right‑side profile.
The ball moves steadily upward relative to the hoop and pole: from rim level (frames 1–20) to above the rim against the pole (frames 21–30) to near the top edge of the backboard (frames 31–41).
The person's guiding arm extends fully upward following the ball, and the body leans back as the ball rises past the hand.

The background hoop, pole and trees keep nearly the same framing throughout, indicating little or no camera movement; the apparent size change of the person is due to their own vertical motion, not a zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the person became airborne and first obtained the ball at the rim before t=0.
What happens to the ball after it reaches the top of the backboard (whether it falls, bounces off, or goes through the hoop) — the clip ends while it is still high and rising.
Whether the person's feet actually touch down or remain just off the ground after the excerpt.
The intent of the action (shot, trick, or staged pose).
uncertain_details: Exact point of release between hand and ball; contact with the pole or backboard cannot be confirmed from the frames.
Whether the camera is perfectly static or has a very slight drift; background parallax is too small to decide.
Precise height of the ball's apex, since it is still ascending at the final frame.
